# Learn TypeScript

## 1. Fundamentals

### 1.1 What is TypeScript
- Superset of JavaScript
- Static typing
- Compiles to JavaScript
- Better tooling & refactoring
- Scalable & maintainable

#### Setup
- Install: `npm install -g typescript`
- Init: `tsc --init`
- Understand `tsconfig.json`
- Enable `"strict": true`

---

### 1.2 Basic Types
- Primitive: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `undefined`, `bigint`, `symbol`
- Special: `any`, `unknown`, `void`, `never`
- Arrays: `T[]`, `Array<T>`
- Tuples: `[T, U]`
- Objects: typed structures
- Functions: params, return, optional, default
- Type aliases
- Interfaces

---

### 1.3 Narrowing
- `typeof`
- `instanceof`
- Equality checks
- Truthiness
- Discriminated unions
- Custom type guards

---

## 2. Core Type System

### 2.1 Unions & Intersections
- Union: `A | B`
- Intersection: `A & B`

### 2.2 Literal Types
- String / number literals
- Safer APIs

### 2.3 Enums
- Numeric
- String
- Prefer union literals

### 2.4 Type Assertions
- `as`
- Use minimally

### 2.5 Modules
- ES Modules
- Type-only imports
- `.d.ts`

---

## 3. Advanced Types

### 3.1 Generics
- Generic functions
- Constraints
- Default types
- Generic interfaces/classes

### 3.2 Utility Types
- `Partial`
- `Required`
- `Readonly`
- `Pick`
- `Omit`
- `Record`
- `Exclude`
- `Extract`
- `NonNullable`
- `ReturnType`
- `Parameters`

### 3.3 Mapped Types
- `[K in keyof T]`

### 3.4 Conditional Types
- `T extends U ? X : Y`
- Distributive behavior

### 3.5 Keyof & Indexed Access
- `keyof`
- `T[K]`

### 3.6 Template Literal Types
- String-based types
- Event-style typing

### 3.7 Infer
- Extract types from generics

---
